page_title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models

sources.entry: A standalone supervised Plan and Solve Agent specialized on performing read and write operations on various tools like GitHub, HubSpot or Airtable _(ACL 2023 Paper "Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models")_

summary.name: Plan-and-Solve Prompting
summary.one_liner: A zero-shot prompting method from a 2023 arXiv paper (ACL 2023) that asks an LLM to devise a plan splitting a task into subtasks and then carry them out, improving on "Let's think step by step" prompting.
keywords: awesome ai agents plan and solve agent
use_cases: improving LLM accuracy on math word problems without examples
prompting LLMs to break tasks into subtasks
reducing missing-step errors in LLM reasoning
building a plan-then-execute prompt for an agent
summary.what_it_does: The paper proposes Plan-and-Solve (PS) Prompting, a zero-shot method where the model first devises a plan dividing the task into smaller subtasks, then carries out those subtasks. It extends this with PS+ prompting, which adds more detailed instructions aimed at reducing calculation errors and improving reasoning step quality. The authors evaluate on ten datasets across three reasoning problem types using GPT-3. They report that PS prompting consistently beats Zero-shot-CoT across all datasets, is comparable to or exceeds Zero-shot Program-of-Thought, and is comparable to 8-shot CoT on math reasoning. Code is linked from the paper's GitHub repository. The arXiv listing also notes that an awesome-ai-agents entry describes a separate agent built on this method for read/write operations on tools such as GitHub, HubSpot and Airtable.
notable: Zero-shot method that needs no manually written demonstrations
PS+ variant adds detailed instructions to reduce calculation errors
Evaluated on ten datasets across three reasoning problem types using GPT-3
Code published at the AGI-Edgerunners GitHub repository
caveats: Experiments were run on GPT-3 only, as stated on the page
Results are reported for reasoning benchmarks; comparison to 8-shot CoT is limited to math reasoning
